question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining a wide base of support during patient transfers?

options.B: To keep the nurse's hands completely free
options.C: To speed up the transfer process
options.D: To increase overall stability and balance

explanation: A wide base of support lowers the center of gravity and prevents the nurse from losing balance during heavy lifts. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why should a nurse avoid twisting the waist while lifting a heavy load?

options.A: It makes communication with the patient difficult
options.B: It places excessive stress on the spinal discs
options.C: It uses up too much physical energy
options.D: It immediately causes the patient to fall backward

explanation: Combining spinal rotation with heavy loads is a primary cause of lower back injury. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h1)

question: What must a nurse assess first before moving a patient from a bed to a chair?

options.A: The patient's ability to bear weight and follow instructions
options.B: The exact weight of the patient in kilograms
options.C: The brand name of the hospital bed
options.D: The color of the patient's room walls

explanation: Knowing a patient's physical capacity helps you decide if they can help or if you need a mechanical lift. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: A patient does about 60% of the physical work during a transfer. How is this level of help classified?
explanation: Moderate assistance is used when the patient performs between 50% and 74% of the physical work needed for the movement. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the first safety check a nurse must do before starting a patient transfer?

options.A: Place a pillow on the wheelchair seat
options.B: Lock the wheels of both the bed and the chair
options.C: Adjust the room lighting to a brighter setting
options.D: Close the room door for privacy

explanation: Unlocked wheels allow furniture to slide apart, which is a common cause of accidental patient falls. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why is a team countdown important when lifting a patient with other staff members?

options.A: It gives the patient time to refuse the movement
options.B: It distracts the patient from feeling sudden pain
options.C: It ensures everyone pulls or lifts at the exact same time

explanation: Counting down together prevents one person from suddenly carrying too much unexpected weight. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h3)

question: At what angle should a wheelchair typically be placed relative to the bed for a safe transfer?
explanation: A 45-degree angle provides the most direct and manageable pathway for a pivot transfer. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h4)

question: A patient with left-sided weakness is moving from a bed to a chair. Where should you place the chair?

options.B: At the foot of the bed facing head-on

explanation: Placing the chair on the stronger side allows the patient to lead with their stronger limbs during the move. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h4)

question: When must a nurse use a mechanical lift instead of a manual transfer?

options.A: When there is only one nurse on duty
options.B: When the patient cannot bear any weight at all
options.C: When the patient has a mild headache
options.D: When the patient prefers to stay in bed all day

explanation: Mechanical lifts are necessary for patients who cannot support their own body weight to keep both patient and nurse safe. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which safety check is essential before using a mechanical floor lift for a patient?

options.A: Checking the expiration date of the hydraulic fluid
options.B: Checking the sling fabric and straps for tears or wear
options.D: Ensuring the lift battery is fully charged

explanation: Damaged slings or frayed straps can snap under pressure and cause a severe fall. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h5)

question: What key detail must you write in the nursing notes after transferring a patient?

options.A: The level of help the patient needed and how they tolerated it
options.B: The exact brand of the wheelchair used
options.D: The name of the doctor who ordered the activity

explanation: Documenting assistance levels helps track patient progress and alerts the next shift to safety needs. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why must you leave the call bell within the patient's reach right after a transfer?

options.A: To comply with hospital design rules
options.B: To let the patient call for help if they feel dizzy or weak
options.C: To let you know when the patient wants to eat
options.D: To keep the patient from falling asleep too quickly

explanation: Quick access to the call bell ensures fast help if the patient experiences sudden dizziness or fatigue after moving. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h6)
